description_full: Piraeus Bank S.A. provides various banking products and services in Greece, Europe, and internationally. The company operates through five segments: Retail Banking, Business Banking, Piraeus Financial Markets, Snappi, and Other. It offers term deposits, savings, current, and payroll and pension accounts; mortgage and personal loans; credit, debit, and prepaid cards; car, civil liability and legal protection, home security, health, pension plans, life and accident, and lifestyle insurance plans; investment products, including savings programs, portfolio management, mutual funds, stock market transactions and services, government bonds and treasury bills, gold investment, and securities custody; and electronic banking services. The company also provides corporate banking products and services, such as professional and farmer accounts; corporate cards; farmer's, business premise, liability, and photovoltaic park insurance plans; and payments and receipts comprising IRIS payments for businesses, business remittance, payment records, collection through bank channels, payroll, accepting cards, money management, checks, and management of bills of exchange. In addition, it offers financing solutions for businesses, which include working capital; professional housing and equipment; co-financed programs, such as farmer financing and specialized solutions; factoring; and letter of guarantee, as well as real estate, equipment, and development leasing. Further, the company provides online stock and bond trading; wealth services comprising investment advice, wealth advisor, multi-family office, execution of transactions, and custody; asset management products, including alternative, structured, and thematic products; and economic and financial planning. It offers its products and services through e-banking, Piraeus app, phone banking, and stores and ATMs. Piraeus Bank S.A. was founded in 1916 and is headquartered in Athens, Greece.

financial_summary: Piraeus Bank S.A. is a large-cap financial services business with a $13.3B market cap on $3.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

The business throws off $2.4B in free cash flow — roughly 81 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.27× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.1% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.
